mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which often precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS is declining, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO > 1% YoY growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS falls > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when both UNRATE and PAYEMS meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) combined with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a disinflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which often correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST > 5% MoM growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising industrial production (INDPRO) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 2% YoY growth and UNRATE falls > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when both INDPRO and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.
